title: dependability-ambassador-rotation-and-collab-schedule-2026
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a lightweight, repeatable Dependability Ambassador rotation to accelerate SLO adoption and reduce first‑time friction for feature teams. Goal is to embed SRE expertise into cross‑functional teams for a time‑boxed window (4–8 weeks) to pair on SLO design, alert tuning, runbook creation, and incident retrospectives.

Context / Why this now
- We keep seeing a long tail for SLO onboarding: teams ship without clear error budgets or meaningful alerts.
- Central SRE team bandwidth is limited; full handoffs rarely happen.
- Feature teams need practical help (not just docs) for pragmatic SLOs and safe rollouts.

High‑level model
- Ambassadors: experienced SREs rotate as "Dependability Ambassadors" into 1–2 product/infra teams for a 6‑week block.
- Ambassadors coach and pair rather than own long‑term ops. After rotation completes, ownership transfers back to the team with followup office hours available.
- Ambassador responsibilities are standardized (below) and supported by templates/automation.

Primary objectives for each rotation
- Ship a minimal, testable SLO for at least one service or route.
- Create a first‑class runbook and escalation path tied to the SLO.
- Tune alerts to reduce noise and ensure actionability.
- Establish a short cadence for SLO signal review and error budget awareness.

Who participates
- Ambassador(s): 1 SRE for small services, 2 SREs for larger or multi‑service initiatives.
- Product/Feature Team: Eng lead, 1 backend engineer, 1 PM, optionally an infra/ops engineer.
- Platform SMEs: console & rollouts, serving runtime engineer (as needed).

Ambassador playbook (checklist)
- Week 0 (prep): review service topology, existing telemetry, past incidents; create a tailored onboarding brief.
- Week 1: workshop SLO candidates with the team; agree on measurable indicators, user‑impact mapping, and target SLOs.
- Week 2: implement basic telemetry (instrumented metrics, dashboards), wire alerting to oncall channel, set initial thresholds.
- Week 3: create runbook skeleton with steps for diagnosis and remediation; run a tabletop exercise.
- Week 4: deploy canary + observability smoke tests; monitor error budget burn and tune alerts.
- Week 5–6: handoff docs, schedule recurrence office hours, train on oncall playbook; capture retro.

Product team onboarding checklist (to be completed during rotation)
- Decide SLO persona (user‑facing latency, correctness, throughput, or dependency SLA).
- Identify primary metric(s) and correct aggregation windows.
- Define error budget policy and allowed remediation behaviors.
- Document post‑mortem and runbook link in the service README.
- Add SLO dashboards to shared console and a lightweight test harness for smoke tests.

Rotation schedule template (6‑week example)
- Week 0: Kickoff + discovery (2h deep dive)
- Week 1: SLO design workshop (3h) + followups (1h/wk)
- Week 2: Implementation sprint pairing (daily 1h sync)
- Week 3: Runbook authoring + tabletop (2h)
- Week 4: Canary rollout + monitoring watch (ad‑hoc)
- Week 5: Stabilization + job to create PRs for docs/alerts
- Week 6: Handoff, retro, and celebration (2h retro)

Lightweight rituals to maintain momentum
- Weekly "SLO signal check" (30m) with metrics and burn rate snapshot.
- Biweekly ambassador office hours (drop‑in for product teams).
- Monthly cross‑team sharing: 20m lightning demos + 10m Q&A.
- Post‑rotation retro recorded and stored in central repo.

Measurement and success criteria
- Time to first SLO (days from kickoff) — target: <= 21 days.
- Percent of rotated teams with an active error budget and runbook after 6 weeks — target: 90%.
- Reduction in noisy alerts from the service during rotation — target: 50% reduction in total alert counts or acknowledged false positives.
- Qualitative: product team reports increased confidence in rollouts (survey).

Escalation & ownership matrix
- During rotation: Ambassador + product team are joint responders for related incidents.
- After rotation: product team owns runbook and SLO; SRE remains primary async reviewer for 30 days and provides oncall support if requested per agreement.
- Severe incident (sev1): follow standard oncall escalation; ambassador involvement optional if still on rotation.

Dependencies & prerequisites for each engagement
- Basic telemetry must exist (counter/captured error metric or latency histogram).
- SRE tooling access (dashboards, alerting config, runbook repo) provisioned ahead of Week 0.
- Clear success criteria chosen by product and ambassador in kickoff.

Automation and templates (to build once)
- SLO starter manifest template (YAML) with guidance comments.
- Runbook markdown template with diagnostic checklist and typical commands.
- Alert tuning cookbook: common patterns (rate vs. absolute, grouping, suppression).
- Standard onboarding brief template for ambassador prep.

Risk & mitigations
- Risk: Ambassador time adds latency to product sprints.
  - Mitigation: Ambassadors pair for short bursts and focus on value milestones (SLO, runbook, alerts).
- Risk: Ownership gaps after handoff.
  - Mitigation: 30‑day async support window and 1 scheduled followup office hour.
- Risk: Scale — SRE capacity limited for many teams concurrently.
  - Mitigation: Prioritize teams by customer impact and run 'train‑the‑trainer' for platform eng to scale.

Budgeting (rough estimate)
- One SRE rotation for 6 weeks ≈ 30–40 person‑days of SRE effort (including prep + followups).
- Expect 6–8 rotations per quarter at current headcount before hiring additional SREs.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Rotation length: 4 vs. 6 vs. 8 weeks — suggest 6 weeks for balance. Owner: Lina Chen.
- SLA for post‑handoff support: what level of free async support vs. paid professional services? Owner: Product leadership (Priya).
- Metrics pipeline gaps: who owns instrumenting missing candidate metrics? Owner: Feature team lead.

Next steps (recommended short list)
- Approve pilot: 3 rotations in Q2 (priority teams to be nominated) — owner: Asha.
- Create the SLO starter manifest and runbook template in repo — owner: Connor.
- Schedule first ambassador office hours and announce to product org — owner: Miguel.
- Add pilot tracking board (Jira DEP‑987) and link retrospective template to Confluence.

Notes to self (workshop fragments)
- Keep SLOs pragmatic: customer observable, tied to clear user journeys.
- Prefer incremental SLOs (start with a high‑level success metric, iterate).
- Make runbooks short, executable checklists — avoid long essays.

Appendix: sample SLO brief (one‑page)
- Service: inference‑gateway
- User journey: request -> response within 500ms 95% of the time for interactive tier
- Metric: p95 latency on successful responses (exclude server errors) aggregated by region per 1m window
- Target: 95% p95 over a 30‑day rolling window
- Error budget: 5% of requests in rolling window; automatic throttling policy when burn exceeds 80%
- Runbook link: {to be created during rotation}
